issues.title: [26.3] Entity vertex buffer grows uncontrollably during raids → 3 FPS, then crash (ByteBufferBuilder max capacity exceeded)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
During village raids, FPS drops from capped 60 to ~15 and eventually ~3 FPS, then the game crashes with `IllegalArgumentException: Maximum capacity of ByteBufferBuilder (4294967295) exceeded`. Outside of raids performance is normal. It continues even with only one raider left.

Spark profiling shows the time is almost entirely spent growing the entity vertex buffer:
- During a stutter: ~90% of render thread time in `ByteBufferBuilder.resize` → `JEmalloc.nje_realloc`, called from `EMFModelPartCustom$EMFCube.compile` → `BufferBuilder.addVertex`. Actual animation work (`ASMAnimationHandler.animateInner`) was only ~1.7%.
- Same area outside the raid: 0% in `ByteBufferBuilder.resize`.
- Entity count was normal (~370 tracked entities, 93 villagers, 73 sheep, 1 vindicator), so this isn't explained by mob count.

Disabling the Fresh Animations resource packs did NOT fix it (still ~3 FPS, then the crash below; that stack trace goes through vanilla `ModelPart.compile` + Sodium's `renderCuboid`). Disabling EMF and ETF fixed it completely: I played through an entire raid (~11.5 min) with no stutter and 0% time in buffer resizing.

**To Reproduce**
1. Join a Realm (vanilla server) with EMF + ETF installed (Fresh Animations on or off).
2. Trigger a raid at a large village (~90 villagers nearby).
3. Watch FPS degrade over the course of the raid. It gets progressively worse until the client crashes.
4. Disable EMF + ETF and repeat: the raid runs normally.

**Expected behavior**
Raids render normally with no runaway vertex buffer growth or crash.

**Screenshots**
N/A. Spark profiles linked below instead.

**Crashlog**
Crash report attached. Key part:
```
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Maximum capacity of ByteBufferBuilder (4294967295) exceeded, required 4294968112
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.ByteBufferBuilder.ensureCapacity(ByteBufferBuilder.java:62)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.ByteBufferBuilder.reserve(ByteBufferBuilder.java:54)
	at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.push(BufferBuilder.java:1557)
	at net.caffeinemc.mods.sodium.client.render.immediate.model.EntityRenderer.renderCuboid(EntityRenderer.java:34)
	at net.minecraft.client.model.geom.ModelPart$Cube.compile(ModelPart.java:324)
	at net.minecraft.client.model.geom.ModelPart.compile(ModelPart.java:192)
	at net.minecraft.client.model.geom.ModelPart.render(ModelPart.java:119)
	at net.minecraft.client.model.Model.renderToBuffer(Model.java:34)
	at net.minecraft.client.renderer.feature.ModelFeatureRenderer.prepareModel(ModelFeatureRenderer.java:39)
	at net.minecraft.client.renderer.feature.ModelFeatureRenderer.buildGroup(ModelFeatureRenderer.java:23)
	...
```
Mixins on the stack include `traben.entity_model_features.mixin.mixins.MixinModelPart$Cuboid`, `MixinModelPart`, `MixinModel`, `Mixin_ModelRenderer`, and `traben.entity_texture_features.mixin.mixins.vertexconsumers.MixinBufferBuilder`.

**(please complete the following information):**
 - Minecraft Version: 26.3 (Fabric Loader 0.19.5, Java 25.0.1)
 - EMF version: 3.3.11 (ETF 7.2.5)
 - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? Not tested yet. It's a Realm raid, so it's hard to reproduce on demand. Disabling EMF + ETF in my full modpack fixed it.
 - Modlist: Fabulously Optimized base (Prism Launcher), plus Sodium 0.9.2, Iris 1.11.7 (no shaders active), ImmediatelyFast 1.17.1, Better Block Entities 1.3.9, Distant Horizons 3.3.4, Xaero's Minimap/World Map, EntityCulling, MoreCulling, ModernFix, Lithium. Full list is in the attached log.

**Additional context**
- Resource packs: Fresh Animations 1.10.5, FA+All_Extensions 1.9.2, FA+Player 1.1
- Hardware: Ryzen 5 9600X, RX 9070 XT, Windows 11 24H2, 10 GB allocated
- Played on a Realm (non-integrated server), not singleplayer
- Attached: crash report
- Spark Profile (EMF/ETF enabled) : https://spark.lucko.me/iPpKhuYmld 
- Spark Profile (EMF/ETF disabled) : https://spark.lucko.me/pxMkLDBs8k

issues.title: [Idea] API request: callback after CEM animation has been applied to the model parts
issues.body:
I maintain Easy NPC. The NPCs reuse vanilla model layers and let users set per-part rotations,
positions, scale and visibility. With a CEM pack loaded those poses are gone, because
`EMFModelPartRoot` does `resetVanillaPartsToDefaults()` and then `animate()` at render time, after
`setupAnim`, where we write ours. (e.g. https://github.com/MarkusBordihn/BOs-Easy-NPC/issues/817)

I don't think either side misbehaves here. Layer-based `.jem` lookup is a feature, and CEM animations
owning the part transforms is the definition of CEM. 
What's missing is a point where a mod can say "this one is user intent, put it on top".
`EMFAnimationApi` doesn't cover it, since the pack decides what it references, and a mixin into EMF internals is what I'd like to avoid: the 26.2 submit refactor already moved that code, and such bridges break on every release.

So: one callback, fired per model after the animation ran and before the parts render.

    EMFAnimationApi.registerPostAnimationListener(
        ResourceLocation id,
        (EMFModelPartRoot root, Object renderState) -> { ... });

Whatever shape is cheapest for you is fine. I need the root part plus enough context to identify the
entity, so I can skip anything that isn't one of my NPCs.

Beyond my own case: stradat maintains a family of "EMF Compat" mods (Not Enough Animations, Better
Combat, Carry On, Create, ...) solving this same problem for the player model, each with its own
mixin into EMF. A supported hook would help to replace those with a few lines each.

Happy to write the PR if you're open to it, just say where the callback should sit.

issues.title: [Bug] Crash or Compatibility
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Game freezes and eventually hard-crashes on the render thread while a monster
spawner's mob preview is being rendered. EMF throws a repeated
`IndexOutOfBoundsException` while writing vertex data for a custom model cube
(`EMFModelPartCustom$EMFCube`), which appears to leave Minecraft's pose stack
unbalanced. About 14 of these exceptions get logged in the same tick, immediately
followed by a fatal `IllegalStateException: Pose stack not empty` on the render
thread, which freezes the game completely (had to be force-closed via Task Manager).

This seems to be very rare, it only happened once in this session, right as a
spawner's preview mob was rendering, and I can't reliably reproduce it on demand.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Load a save with a monster spawner nearby whose preview entity uses a custom
   (CEM) model via EMF/ETF.
2. Be in render range while the spawner renders its spinning mob preview.
3. Crash occurs spontaneously (no direct player action needed), could not
   reliably reproduce a second time.
4. See error / freeze.

**Expected behavior**
Spawner preview renders normally without corrupting the pose stack.

**Screenshots**
N/A (game froze, no visual glitch before the freeze).

**Crashlog**
See attached `latest.log`. Relevant section starts at the first
`IndexOutOfBoundsException` in `EMFModelPartCustom$EMFCube`, ends with:

```
[Render thread/ERROR] [net.minecraft.client.Minecraft/FATAL]: Unreported exception thrown!
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Pose stack not empty
at net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.m_109588_(LevelRenderer.java:1431)
at net.minecraft.client.renderer.LevelRenderer.m_109599_(LevelRenderer.java:1282)
at net.minecraft.client.renderer.GameRenderer.m_109089_(GameRenderer.java:1126)
at net.minecraft.client.renderer.GameRenderer.m_109093_(GameRenderer.java:909)
at net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.m_91383_(Minecraft.java:1146)
```


**(please complete the following information):**
 - Minecraft Version: 1.20.1
 - Forge Version: 47.4.23
 - EMF version: 3.3.5
 - ETF version: 7.2.1
 - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed?: Not tested yet, happened in a
   large modpack.
 - if applicable, provide your modlist or log: https://mclo.gs/joA3vSQ

**Additional context**
The exception fires inside `SpawnerRenderer` -> `EntityRenderDispatcher` ->
`MobRenderer`, i.e. while rendering the mob preview inside a monster spawner block,
not a "live" mob in the world. The repeated `IndexOutOfBoundsException` on the
vertex buffer suggests the custom model for whatever entity was in the spawner had
more vertices/cubes than the allocated buffer expected. The thrown exception then
appears to skip the matching `popPose()` call, corrupting the pose stack for the
rest of the frame and crashing the render thread shortly after.

issues.title: [Bug] OOM: vertex buffer grows to ~488 MB during EMF model part rendering (EMF 3.2.6, MC 26.2)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

While walking around a normal world, a single vertex buffer grows until it hits ~488 MB and the
game dies with an `OutOfMemoryError`. The JVM heap is nowhere near full when this happens (~26% of
6 GB in use), so this is not heap exhaustion — it is one native `ByteBufferBuilder` receiving an
enormous number of vertices during EMF model part rendering.

Before the crash the symptoms are ~30 FPS in an ordinary village with shaders **off**, on an RTX
5060 / Ryzen 7 5800X, and stuttering that worsens as more mobs come into view.

**To Reproduce**

1. Install EMF 3.2.6 + ETF 7.1.1 on Minecraft 26.2 (Fabric).
2. Enable FreshAnimations 1.10.5 with FA+Player 1.1, FA+Objects 2.1.2, FA+Details 2.3.
3. Load a world and walk around a village so mobs keep entering view.
4. FPS degrades, then the "Out of memory" screen appears.

I have not yet narrowed it to a specific entity — happy to bisect the FA add-on packs or turn on
`logModelCreationData` and capture a more detailed run if that would help.

**Expected behavior**

Entity rendering should not accumulate hundreds of megabytes of vertex data in one buffer.

**Crashlog**

```
[Render thread/ERROR]: Out of memory
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Failed to resize buffer from 488636416 bytes to 490733568 bytes
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.ByteBufferBuilder.resize(ByteBufferBuilder.java:77)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.ByteBufferBuilder.ensureCapacity(ByteBufferBuilder.java:66)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.ByteBufferBuilder.reserve(ByteBufferBuilder.java:54)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.beginVertex(BufferBuilder.java:128)
    at com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.BufferBuilder.addVertex(BufferBuilder.java:308)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartCustom$EMFCube.compile(EMFModelPartCustom.java:449)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.compile(EMFModelPart.java:544)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderLikeVanilla(EMFModelPart.java:346)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderTextureOverrideWithoutReset(EMFModelPart.java:310)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderWithTextureOverride(EMFModelPart.java:261)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartCustom.renderWithTextureOverride(EMFModelPartCustom.java:197)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.render(EMFModelPart.java:88)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartCustom.render(EMFModelPartCustom.java:168)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderLikeVanilla(EMFModelPart.java:356)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderLikeETF(EMFModelPart.java:426)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderWithTextureOverride(EMFModelPart.java:213)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartCustom.renderWithTextureOverride(EMFModelPartCustom.java:197)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.render(EMFModelPart.java:88)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartCustom.render(EMFModelPartCustom.java:168)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderLikeVanilla(EMFModelPart.java:356)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderLikeETF(EMFModelPart.java:426)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPart.renderWithTextureOverride(EMFModelPart.java:213)
    ... this block repeats for dozens more frames ...
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartWithState.render(EMFModelPartWithState.java:50)
    at traben.entity_model_features.models.parts.EMFModelPartVanilla.render(EMFModelPartVanilla.java:73)
```

**What stands out**

The cycle `render -> renderLikeVanilla -> renderLikeETF -> renderWithTextureOverride -> render`
repeats many times within one stack. At roughly 28-32 bytes per vertex, 488 MB is on the order of
15 million vertices — hundreds of thousands of cubes for entity rendering in a single buffer.
That points to either re-entrant rendering of the same parts, or a buffer that is not being
flushed/reset between entities, rather than to a legitimately deep model.

**(please complete the following information):**

- Minecraft Version: 26.2 (Fabric Loader 0.19.3, Java 25)
- EMF version: 3.2.6 (ETF 7.1.1)
- Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? **Not tested yet** — this is a ~200 mod pack.
  I can test an EMF+ETF-only instance if that would be useful.
- Modlist: large pack; the rendering-relevant parts are Sodium, Iris (shaders disabled),
  Nvidium 0.4.4-beta4, Lithium, ImmediatelyFast.

**Additional context**

- JVM: `-Xms1G -Xmx6G -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:+DisableExplicitGC`. Heap usage was ~26% (1619/6144 MB) at
  the time, with an allocation rate of ~107 MB/s.
- EMF config: `renderModeChoice: NORMAL`, `allowedCEM: ALL`, `modelUpdateFrequency: Average`,
  `animationLODDistance: 20`, `retainDetailOnLowFps: true`, `retainDetailOnLargerMobs: true`.
- ETF config: `enableCustomTextures`, `enableEmissiveTextures`, `skinFeaturesEnabled` all on,
  which is presumably why the `renderLikeETF` branch is in the path.
- Happy to provide the full `latest.log` or run any diagnostic build.

issues.title: [Bug] Crash or Compatibility
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
After updating **Entity Model Features (EMF) from 3.2.6 to 3.3**, Minecraft crashes every time I try to enter a world when **Elytra Contrails Mod** is installed.

This issue did not occur with **EMF 3.2.6**.

I tested this using the exact same Minecraft installation, world, mod list, and Elytra Contrails version:

* **EMF 3.3 installed** → entering a world causes an immediate crash.
* **Downgrading EMF back to 3.2.6** → the same world loads normally again.

Nothing else was changed between the two tests.

This is therefore a regression introduced in **EMF 3.3**, affecting compatibility with Elytra Contrails.

---

**To Reproduce**

1. Install Minecraft **26.2** with Fabric Loader.
2. Install **EMF 3.3**.
3. Install **Elytra Contrails Mod 1.5.2-26.2**.
4. Launch Minecraft.
5. Open Singleplayer.
6. Select a world.
7. Attempt to enter the world.
8. Minecraft crashes during world loading.

To confirm the regression:

9. Replace **EMF 3.3** with **EMF 3.2.6**.
10. Keep all other mods and settings unchanged.
11. Launch Minecraft again.
12. Enter the exact same world.
13. The world loads normally without crashing.

---

**Expected behavior**
The world should load normally with EMF and Elytra Contrails installed together, as it does with **EMF 3.2.6**.

Updating EMF from 3.2.6 to 3.3 should not cause Minecraft to crash when entering a world.

---

**Screenshots**
Not applicable.

---

**Crashlog**
I can provide the crash report and/or `latest.log`.

---

**(please complete the following information):**

* Minecraft Version: **26.2**
* Mod Loader: **Fabric**
* EMF version: **3.3**
* Previous working EMF version: **3.2.6**
* Elytra Contrails version: **1.5.2-26.2**
* Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? **No. The crash occurs when EMF 3.3 is used together with Elytra Contrails.**
* Does downgrading EMF fix the issue? **Yes. Downgrading from EMF 3.3 to 3.2.6 completely fixes the crash without changing anything else.**
* Modlist or log: **Can be provided.**

---

**Additional context**
This is a reproducible regression introduced in **EMF 3.3**.

My setup was working normally with **EMF 3.2.6** and Elytra Contrails installed together.

After updating only EMF to **3.3**, Minecraft began crashing every time I attempted to enter a world.

I then downgraded only EMF back to **3.2.6**, without changing:

* Minecraft version
* Fabric Loader
* the world
* Elytra Contrails
* resource packs
* or any other installed mods

After downgrading, the crash disappeared immediately and the same world loaded normally again.

The conflicting mod is:

**Elytra Contrails Mod (elytratrails) 1.5.2-26.2**

This behavior can be consistently reproduced by switching between:

**EMF 3.3 → crash when entering world**

and

**EMF 3.2.6 → world loads normally**

issues.title: Empty-hand first-person arm animation (FA+Player) causes missing-texture block-break particles on modded crops
issues.body:
Environment:

Minecraft: 1.20.1 / Forge: 47.4.20
EMF: entity_model_features-3.2.4-1.20.1-forge
ETF: entity_texture_features_1.20.1-forge-7.1 (installed, confirmed unrelated)
Embeddium 0.3.31 + Oculus 1.8.0
Resource packs: FreshAnimations_v1.10.4.zip, FA+Player-v1.0.zip
Supplementaries-1.20-3.1.43-forge (provides the flax crop)
______________________________________________________________________________
Steps to reproduce:

Install FA + FA+Player as active resource packs on Forge 1.20.1 with EMF + Oculus + Embeddium.
Grow a Supplementaries flax crop to full maturity.
With an empty hand, harvest the flax.
Observe the block-break particles: missing-texture placeholder instead of the flax sprite.
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________
Ruled out:
Supplementaries' own assets (decompiled, all references resolve)

Other resource packs (reproduces with FA alone; isolating to FA+Player specifically confirms/denies it)

ETF (FA+Player depends only on EMF; still reproduces with ETF disabled)

Pure Oculus atlas capacity (doesn't explain the empty-hand-vs-held-item split)
______________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Suspected mechanism:
player.jem/player_slim.jem branch arm-bone formulas on is_first_person_hand, pulling from a_player_firstperson.jpm — active only during empty-hand first-person rendering. Suspect a texture-bind/state leak in that path bleeding into the same-frame particle draw call.
______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
What I tried
Stripped the is_first_person_hand branches entirely (fallback to third-person formula always) — stopped the particle bug, but broke all third-person animation, despite valid JSON. Suggests EMF rejects/falls back the whole model on some condition beyond syntax validity. Can share the diff if useful.

issues.title: Fresh Animations / FA Player + EMF animation desync when aiming/shooting bows in third person
issues.body:
Environment

Minecraft version:

1.20.1

Mods / packs used:

EMF
ETF
Fresh Animations / FA Player
Multiple third person camera mods
Vanilla third person also tested

Third person mods tested:

Leawind Third Person
Other third person camera mods
Summary

There appears to be a player arm animation desync/glitch related to bow usage in third person.

The issue is especially easy to trigger when using third person camera mods such as Leawind Third Person, but it can still occur even without those mods installed.

After extensive testing, the problem seems more related to Fresh Animations / FA Player animation handling or EMF interpolation behavior rather than a specific third person mod alone.

Fresh Moves was tested under the same conditions and does NOT appear to have this issue.

Reproduction
Vanilla third person
Enter third person
Aim a bow
Rapidly turn the camera with large yaw movement
Release the arrow while rotating
With third person camera mods installed

The issue becomes much easier to reproduce.

With Leawind Third Person specifically:

simply shooting arrows several times in third person is often enough to trigger the bug consistently
Result

Player arm animations can visibly break/desync:

arm twisting
shoulder snapping
jittering
incorrect arm poses
stretched-looking arms

The issue appears to happen during fast yaw rotation while bow pose animations are active.

Important observation

Fresh Moves does not seem to suffer from the same issue under identical testing conditions.

This makes me suspect the problem may specifically involve:

FA Player arm sway expressions
FA Player interpolation logic
bow pose handling during rapid yaw changes
interaction with EMF interpolation

rather than EMF alone.

Additional observations

At first I believed Leawind Third Person was directly causing the issue.

However:

the same bug can still happen in vanilla third person
the same bug can also be reproduced with other third person camera mods

Leawind simply seems to amplify the issue and make it much easier to trigger.

Possible cause (theory)

My current theory is:

Vanilla bow poses update arm rotations instantly, while FA Player dynamic arm sway/interpolation continues applying additional offsets during rapid camera movement and arrow release.

This may become unstable during large yaw transitions, especially near angle wraparound situations such as:

180° → -180°

Potentially related systems:

EMF interpolation
FA Player expressions
body yaw / head yaw synchronization
arm sway smoothing
pose blending
Request

If possible, I would really appreciate:

confirmation whether this is a known issue
help identifying which FA Player expressions may be responsible
or a possible compatibility fix/workaround

I genuinely love:

Leawind Third Person’s free camera movement
Fresh Animations / FA Player’s expressive animations

and would really love to see them work smoothly together.

issues.title: [Bug] Compatibility issue with Punchy
issues.body: Hello, I've came across a visual bug that occurs when using EMF 3.2.4 alongside Fresh Animations and the Punchy mod on Minecraft 1.21.1 Fabric. When multiple entities or only **one of any type are on screen**, one of them will have its limbs visually broken or flying out of position, the rest of the group displays perfectly normal animations and models. The problem only appears when the affected entity is visible on screen, which suggests it is happening during rendering rather than during game logic. I've already tried adjusting EMF's config file, modifying mod load order, and reviewing available config options in EMF 3.2.4. None of these resolved the issue. Punchy does not appear to show a configuration file that would allow disabling its animation modifications per entity type. I wanted to flag this in case EMF's shared instance behaviour is something that could be made more resilient to external transform modifications, or in case this is a known interaction that has a workaround I have missed. I was unable to locate a public repository for Punchy to report this there first. Happy to provide any additional information or testing if it helps.

issues.body: **Describe the bug** Basically, with EMF and ISMAH installed, if a player gets hit by an arrow, that arrow renders in first-person view regardless of which part of the body it pierced. I've included extra context at the end. Requires the use of a resource pack that applies first-person player animations, such as FA+Player or Fresh Moves. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Receive arrows, whether from an entity or a dispenser. **Expected behavior** All arrows embedded in the player's body are rendered in first person, rather than just those in the visible arm. **Screenshots** **(please complete the following information):** - Minecraft Version: all - EMF Version: all - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? **Describe the bug**

issues.title: [Idea] New Feature - Checking for specific item in hand
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I tried to edit the code in the Detailed Animations resource pack's player.jem file with the help of AI, because I have no one to ask for advice/help on how to change the code (and I don't know where to ask for help or if anyone is even remotely interested in helping me with this).
I wanted to make the resource pack better compatible with the First Person mod and the Not Enough Animations mod. My goal was it to suppress the animation of the arm, that is holding a torch, for beginnings.
Gemini suggested to add this as a variable to test for it:
```
"var.is_holding_light_right": "if(main_hand_item == 'minecraft:torch', 1, 0)",
"var.is_holding_light_left": "if(off_hand_item == 'minecraft:torch', 1, 0)"
```
Or, now at the end...:
```
"var.is_holding_light_right": "if(main_hand_item_id == 'torch', 1, 0)",

```
"var.is_holding_item_right": "if(is_holding_item_right, 1, 0)",
"var.is_holding_item_left": "if(is_holding_item_left, 1, 0)",

issues.title: [Bug - models]models.N in Random Entity properties silently invalidates the whole file when N > 10 for some entities

labels.name: Added / Fixed in next release
labels.description: This tag should be automatically removed upon the next release

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When using OptiFine-style Random Entity .properties files to select CEM/JEM models, the entire properties file is silently ignored if a models.N entry uses an index greater than 10 for certain entities (confirmed with armor_stand).

For example, adding a single line like:

models.11=1001


causes the whole .properties file to be treated as if it does not exist, even if all other rules (models.1–models.10) are valid.
This behavior is inconsistent across entities.
For instance, trapped_chest works correctly with models.N values up to at least models.19, while armor_stand fails as soon as models.11 is present.
No error or warning is shown to the user; the file is simply ignored.

**List and link to broken resourcepacks**
Not publicly published yet.
The issue is reproducible with a minimal test resource pack using:

assets/minecraft/optifine/random/entity/armorstand/wood.properties (required without any valid functions.)
assets/minecraft/optifine/cem/armor_stand.properties

Minimal repro example:

models.1=1001
nbt.1.ArmorItems.3.id=minecraft:knowledge_book

models.11=1001


→ The entire properties file is ignored.

**Expected behavior**
In OptiFine, models.N indices are not documented as being limited to 10, and higher indices should either:

work correctly, or be ignored individually with a warning, without invalidating the entire .properties file.
At the very least, the presence of models.N where N > 10 should not cause all other valid rules in the file to be discarded.

**Screenshots**
N/A (the issue manifests as the properties file being completely ignored with no visible error output).

**(please complete the following information):**
Minecraft Version: 1.20.6
EMF version: 2.4.1
ETF version: 6.2.9

**Additional context**
This issue is reproducible even if models.11 is the only additional line added.
Skipping rule numbers (e.g. models.1 and models.5) works as long as the index is ≤ 10.
The problem appears to be entity-specific:
armor_stand fails at models.11, while trapped_chest works with at least up to models.19.
This suggests a hardcoded or per-entity upper bound for model indices, rather than a general Random Entity limitation.
Expanding or unifying the allowed models.N range (or at least failing gracefully with warnings instead of invalidating the entire file) would significantly improve compatibility with large-scale CEM setups.

issues.title: [Suggestion] .properties for jpms
issues.body: Got this idea while trying to help someone on discord. A model that reference a jpm could have that jpm variate through a .propertie file. Example: Benefits? First, in my case: Currently working on my villagers packs. On 1.21.9+ they don't display jobs and biome when the model has a texture override. I use jpms in every part to bring them. But there are 14 professions (just vanilla) that is at least 14 cubes per body part (wich are body, left arm, right arm, head, left leg, right leg)... so it is 84 cubes, even more in fact (2nd layer stuff and hats) There is also the same for the 5 job levels.... and the 7 biomes Each cube in the jpm has his own texture override to the vanilla texture. Then a bit of math with nbt check to make visible only tu cube for the corresponding job. This does works, and this is fully compatible with other job textures ressource pack, however this is not great for performances... Even if a lot of cubes are not visible I feel the lag with small amount of villagers on my not so bad pc already... By having a way to variate the jpms with a .properties, this should reduce the number of cubes loaded drasticlly and improve perfs as only one cube of the one jpm that woud load. I also have an idea for another pack that will soon make heavy use of jpms with lots of cube to only display one each time. This method would make it virtualy expandable to the infinity... (and beyond! :p) for a fraction of the perfs... I'm sure this could be use for other things too. Just another way to add random stuff in the models Please don't tell me this is already possible. I tried it as you see in the example and it wasn't working (but I'm also very tired 😅,so maybe I'm just an idiot. I actually post this right before bed!) ^^

labels.name: Added / Fixed in next release
labels.description: This tag should be automatically removed upon the next release

issues.body: **Describe the bug** I was testing resourcepacks on my modpack and was wondering why the framerate dropped signifigantly. After profiling with spark, i noticed that EMF was being absurdly slow. I managed to isolate the issue to an replicatable instance. Turns out, if you run Beefier Bovine x Fresh Animation resourcepack, with Oculus shaders enabled, your framerate will tank to an absurd degree when you are looking at more than 30 mobs (From 165 to 40) If you disable shaders or swap the resource pack to Beefier Bovine (The non Fresh Animations version), the framerate will stay stable. **To Reproduce** 1. Download Fresh Animations, Beefier Bovine and Beefier Bovine x Fresh Animations 2. Install Embeddium and Occulus 3. Download ComplimnetaryReimagined Shaders 4. Go ingame, enable Beefier Bovine x Fresh Animations and Fresh Animations resourcepacks (Beefier Bovine x Fresh Animations ABOVE Fresh Animations) and Shaders 5. Create a world and spawn 30 cows in a hole 6. Looking at the cows should tank your framerate 7. Disable Shaders or swap the the resourcepack to the normal version of Beefier Bovine 8. Your framerate should be stable **Expected behavior** The framerate stays stable **Screenshots** With Beefier Bovine x Fresh Animation, shaders enabled: With Beefier Bovine, shaders enabled: **(please complete the following information):** - Minecraft Version: 1.20.1 - EMF version: 3.0.1 - Entity Texture Features: 7.0.2 - Embeddium: 0.3.31+mc1.20.1 - Oculus: mc1.20.1-1.8.0 - Spark: 1.10.53-forge - Fresh Animations: 1.10.1 BETA - Beefier Bovine x Fresh Animations: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/beefier-bovine-x-fresh-animations - Beefier Bovine: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/beefier-bovine - ComplimentaryReimagined: 5.6.1 (https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/shaders/complementary-reimagined/files/7090226) - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed?: No (As in, having ONLY EMF doesent cause issues) **Additional context** Log: [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23123166/latest.log) Spark: https://spark.lucko.me/rsstwSywiE

issues.body: Must be kinda the same thing than #364 (better to get a read on there first as I use the same pack/parts to describe this issue) I was trying to get a workaround. My idea was to get rid of the main texture.properties by making different models with the main texture override unique to them. Then the cape part would match the `modelsuffix` instead of the texture to get his texture applicate. This is actually working with this configuration: Villager.properties ```properties models.2= 2 3 4 5 weights.2= 1 1 1 1 models.3= 2 3 4 5 weights.3= 1 1 1 1 nbt.3.SleepingX=exists:true ``` Cape.properties ```properties modelSuffix.1=5 skins.1=1 modelSuffix.2=2 skins.2=2 modelSuffix.3=3 skins.3=3 modelSuffix.4=4 skins.4=4 ``` Now, if I set the cape.properties this way with only model 5 of villager in the villager.propertie then it also does work as intended ```properties modelSuffix.2=5 skins.2= 1 2 3 4 weights.2= 1 1 1 1 ``` However, If I set models 2 & 5 for the villagers, and the following for the cape, then the cape only ever get only one color per model. ```properties modelSuffix.2=5 skins.2= 1 4 weights.2= 1 1 modelSuffix.3=2 skins.3= 2 3 weights.3= 1 1 ``` And when the cape.propertie try to set the four colors at random for both models, it only apply to of them per model ```propertie modelSuffix.2=5 skins.2= 1 2 3 4 modelSuffix.3=2 skins.3= 1 2 3 4 ``` Here is the pack for testing [models villagers.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21765128/models.villagers.zip) On a side note related to #363 using model with suffix different from 1 seems to make it that NO layers is displayed. issues.title: [Bug] Crash - IllegalStateException: Not Building
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
After much trial and error, I've boiled down an issue with EMF(possibly including ETF) and Mob Battle Mod. While holding one of the mod's tools (Armor Edit tool) and moving/hovering over skeletons, the game crashes or freezes. I initially reported this on[ Mob Battle Mod's issue tracker](https://github.com/Flemmli97/MobBattle/issues/58) as I could not initially figure out why this was occurring or if it was occurring due to a mod clash, which felt impossible as I had not updated any mods between that day and the day before when I played. However, I have narrowed the issue down to EMF/ETF and something to do with the entity rendering.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. With EMF, ETF, and Mob Battle Mod installed, have the Armor Edit tool in your hand
2. Attempt to hover over skeletons (in testing, a singular skeleton in an area did not cause issues, it only became an issue when multiple were in a single area.)
3. Game either will freeze or will crash to desktop before reaching the point when you hover over and highlight the skeleton in front of you

**Expected behavior**
I have had EMF/ETF and Mob Battle Mod for quite a while now, among other mods, and the expected behavior is that I can right-click mobs (shift-right click in the case of Villagers) with the Armor Edit Tool in order to edit their armor inventory.

**Screenshots**
Can't really screenshot a freeze/crash

**Crashlog**
With just EMF, ETF, and Mob Battle Mod:
[crash-2025-08-04_22.14.01-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21588664/crash-2025-08-04_22.14.01-client.txt)
Error log that resulted in a freeze, above mods plus addition during 50-50 testing:
https://gist.github.com/burghenby/349c8561765df35832e30903260fcaf2
Initial crash log that started it all:
[crash-2025-08-03_21.08.36-client.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21588736/crash-2025-08-03_21.08.36-client.txt)

**(please complete the following information):**
 - Minecraft Version: 1.21.1
 - EMF version: 2.4.1
 - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? No, it only occurs when paired with Mob Battle Mod
 - Mod List as of Final Crash: EMF, ETF 6.2.9, Mob Battle Mod 2.6.2 (Full mod list can be found in initial crash log)

**Additional context**
As mentioned above, this has also been posted in the Mob Battle Mod issue tracker. I've also, as of typing this section, had a brainwave. I rolled Mob Battle Mod back a couple more versions and discovered the issue is specifically with the versions from 2.6.0 and up. My theory (which I shared to Mob Battle's issue tracker) is that whatever they did to add the highlight mechanic when hovering over a mob with their tools is causing the incompatibility with EMF's entity rendering. But I don't know what that is, that's way over my head. It does mean that I hadn't encountered the issue until now purely by chance and that I can safely continue using the mod with an older version.

issues.title: [Idea] Support for animated textures for custom entity models.
issues.body:
I was trying to troubleshoot why my textures weren't animating on my model even though I seem to have done everything right. That was until I decided to double check with Optifine and saw that animated textures just weren't supported in ETF.

It'd be nice if ETF had functionality with Optifine's "anim" folder and .properties files.

Within Optifine, .properties files are formated as such:
from=<path to animation>
to=<path to texture to animate>
x=<x coordinate of area to animate>
y=<y coordinate of area to animate>
w=<width of area to animate>
h=<height of area to animate>
duration=<default frame duration in ticks>
interpolate=<true|false>
skip=<interpolation ticks to skip>

(If there's a different way to get animated textures working on custom models, please let me know. I've been at this for a few hours.)

I hope I'll explain this one clearly! :p 
Guard villagers are not made by the same person on Neo vs Fabric. On forge they recently added the biome specific layer via a subfloder biome with a base texture in the guardvillagers texture folder (same logic than villagers). On fabric, there is just 6 textures in the texture folder.
On my guards I have their weapons on custom locations on the body rather than held in hand. To do this, I have the arms were the weapon is held with no cubes, and a set of fake arms.

For my maths, the fake arms follow the vanilla ones all the time, and the normal arms will follow the vanilla behavior if agressive, or have a custom location (set by variables).
For the armor to match the fake arms, I set some variables that just copy the fake arms that I call in the armor_layers.jem.

textureSuffix.1=1

textureSuffix.2=2

skins.3=3

issues.title: Armor NBT/Components for .properties from its item data
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The custom model feature for the armor is a really cool unique feature, but it is now a little limited. I saw the request for new attributes in the properties file, but perhaps just connecting armor components/NBT to armor equipment would work better? At the moment, the mod can't read any NBT data from armor (or if it exists in the game at all), or I have tried badly. This will greatly facilitate the creation of resource packs for modifying multiple armors with one resource pack. Some things are possible with the help of animation, but not everything, such as getting information about renaming or enchantments (even if there was one, it used a non-existent tag), especially in the interval between versions 1.21.2 and 1.21.4, where there are no workarounds - CIT Resewn was not updated to versions higher than 1.21.1, and the official function of interaction with components came out later, 1.21.5

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add the ability for the armor to read the NBT/component data of its item through a file.properties (they work, they just try to read data from the armor, which, as I understand it, does not exist)

**Does OptiFine do this**
No

issues.title: 1.21 Components in .properties support
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
OptiFine has added the new system for resource packs which supports components, so some new packs can use them instead (as OptiFine recommends them in the documentation, and the NBT category is no longer highlighted, there will be more and more component packs). But EMF and ETF don't support them.
So, instead of nbt.n.tag, people will start using components.n.tag (if they haven’t started already).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a45288da-7cec-42c9-b655-f4797a089cc9)
random_entities.properties still has NBT mentions, but it calls us in cit_single.properties https://github.com/sp614x/optifine/blob/master/OptiFineDoc/doc/random_entities.properties

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/790627a3-5a1b-43a0-9024-6fc5e0fe7b50)
In cit_single.properties, components are highlighted https://github.com/sp614x/optifine/blob/master/OptiFineDoc/doc/cit_single.properties

issues.title: [Bug] Rendering Issue with Translucent Outer Layer and Glowing Inner Layer on Player Skins in Minecraft 1.21.2+
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
In Minecraft 1.21.1 and below, this issue does not occur under normal circumstances. However, starting from 1.21.2 and above, a rendering bug affects player skins when using the Fabric loader (tested with version 0.16.10) and the latest Fabric API.
**Issue Details**
The player skin consists of two layers: an inner layer and an outer layer, where the outer layer can contain translucent pixels (colored pixels with an alpha value less than 255).
If an inner layer pixel is set to glowing, and the corresponding outer layer pixel is translucent, then the inner layer pixel becomes invisible in-game, creating a hole in the skin.
Similarly, if the outer layer pixel is set to glowing, and the corresponding inner layer pixel is translucent, then the inner layer pixel is also invisible, but the outer layer remains visible and glowing.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1.Install Minecraft 1.21.2 or later with Fabric Loader 0.16.10 and the latest Fabric API.
2.Use a custom player skin with:
A translucent outer layer (alpha < 255).
A normal inner layer in the same area.
3.set glowing pixels on inner layer.
4.Observe that the inner layer pixels are not rendered in the game, leaving holes in the skin.
5.Swap the glow effect to the outer layer instead and observe the same issue—the inner layer disappears, but the outer layer remains glowing.

**Expected behavior**
the inner layer should be visible


**Screenshots**
below is bug screenshot,there's hole on player's face
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e29e3a29-bdba-457a-be33-62c2209a3dc2)
below is normal screenshot,player's eye should be glowing and visible
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11787cce-9598-430d-967a-e8d7d7d038bf)


**Crashlog**
This issue does not cause crashes, and no error logs are generated.

**(please complete the following information):**
 - Minecraft Version: 1.21.2 and later
 - EMF version 2.4.1
 - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? yes
 - if applicable, provide your modlist or log

**Additional context**
In Minecraft 1.21.1 or lower, this issue does not normally occur. However, when this mod is used alongside certain other mods, the rendering issue can also appear, even in older versions.
This suggests a possible conflict between rendering methods used by different mods.
For example,add emf to betterMC [BMC4] v35.5 1.20.1 will cause render issue too

issues.title: [UUID namespace] UUID namespace for player models
issues.body:
**Describe the solution you'd like**
A UUID namespace for `random_entities.properties.`
If you place a player's UUID (unique user identification) in a `player.properties` file located in the `assets/<NAMESPACE>/optifine/cem/player` folder and add entries like the following:
```
skins.<n>=<N>
uuid.<n>=<UUID>
```
Then, when a player adds the pack, the skin corresponding to the uuid that matches the player's UUID in the properties will be used (i.e., models.<n>).


**Does OptiFine do this**
No

issues.title: [Bug - models] [1.21.4] Baby villagers inconsistently use the vanilla model.
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
This issue is new to MC 1.21.4. It does not occur in MC 1.21.3, and sounds different from the baby issues mentionned in the pinned post.

Baby villagers can usually use the non-`_baby` versions of the villager models. However, if there exists is a `villager.properties` (even an empty one), then model n°1 will use the vanilla model instead of the regular custom model. Other numbered models seem to work fine.

For example:
```properties
# Both babies and adults use `villager2.jem`
models.1=2 
nbt.1.SleepingX=exists:true

# Adults use `villager.jem`, but Babies use the vanilla model.
# (This bit is implied, removing it from the file doesn't change the behaviour.)
models.2=1
```
![Observed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/742515e9-3355-4e0a-bcc7-bfe4dd719f66)

**List and link to broken resourcepacks**
This is based on [Human-Era-Villagers](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/human-era-villagers-illagers/), but here's the smallest pack required to reproduce the issue: [hev-debug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18308435/hev-debug.zip)


**Expected behavior**
![Expected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04a6a36a-0d86-4a97-868e-08b3d37005a2)
This is how the same pack behaved in MC 1.21.3. This behaviour can still be achieved, by renaming `villager.jem` to `villager3.jem`, and using these properties:
```properties
models.1=2 
nbt.1.SleepingX=exists:true

models.2=3
```

Alternatively, I'd need to provide identical `_baby` copies of **both** `villager.jem` and `villager2.cem`. (Providing a `villager_baby` without a `_baby2` would cause the sleeping model to fail instead, but I believe that's expected in this case ?)



**(please complete the following information):**
 - Minecraft Version: 1.21.4
 - EMF version: 1.21.4-2.4.1
 - ETF version if applicable: 1.21.4-6.2.10

**Additional context**
I'm not familiar with the Optifine format at all; me forking this pack is basically my first experience of it. I've skimmed through the relevant documentation, but please point out the obvious if I'm missing anything.

When using the option "show debug data on right-click", on 1.21.4, clicking a baby villager lists both the baby and the regular models. On 1.21.3, only the regular model is listed.

issues.title: [Bug] Skin issue when used with ETF and Xaero's Minimap/World Map
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When EMF is used along with ETF and Xaero's Minimap/WorldMap, the client player's skin is applied to every player entity in the world after reloading resourcepacks (F3+T)

**To Reproduce**
1. Connect to a server
2. Enable Player skin features
3. Wait for the first resourcepack reload
4. Go back, do the second reload
5. Other player entities now display the client player's skin

**Expected behavior**
Other player entities will display their skin instead of the client player's. 

**Video about this issue**
https://youtu.be/DXLUioUhzMs

**Crashlog**
latest.log: https://mclo.gs/HDg2wpu

**(please complete the following information):**
 - Minecraft Version: 1.21.4
 - EMF version: 2.4.1
 - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? -- sort of?
 - Mods:
   - Entity Model Features 2.4.1
   - Entity Texture Features 6.2.9
   - Fabric API 0.114.0+1.21.4
   - ModMenu 13.0.0-beta.1
   - Xaero's Minimap 24.7.1
   - Xaero's WorldMap 1.39.2

**Additional context**
This issue doesn't seem to exist when only ETF is installed, so I guess this is an EMF issue?

issues.title: [Bug] Crash with EMFAnimationApi.registerSingletonAnimationVariable
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Calling `EMFAnimationApi.registerSingletonAnimationVariable` with a `FloatSupplier` crashes the game

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Register a singleton float variable by calling the `registerSingletonAnimationVariable` function with a `FloatSupplier`
2. Launch the game

**Expected behavior**
It shouldn't crash (and also should register the variable)

**Crashlog**
If applicable, add your crashlog or latest.log to help explain your problem.

 - Minecraft Version: [1.21.4]
 - EMF version [2.4.1]
 - Does the issue persist with only EMF installed? Yes
 - [latest.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18223624/latest.log)

**Additional context**
Likely cause of the issue: 
Line 86 of `EMFAnimationAPI`
`VariableRegistry.getInstance().registerSimpleFloatVariable(variableName, variableExplanationTranslationKeyOrText, (MathValue.ResultSupplier) variableValueSupplier);`
The `variableValueSupplier`, which does not inherit from `MathValue.ResultSupplier`, is forcibly cast to it, producing a `ClassCastException`

I maintain an EMF and a vanilla version of my server resource pack. Currently, I send the EMF version by default and when users complain about broken models, they can use a command to opt out and use the vanilla version.
This may be detrimental to the new-player experience.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
If the mod identifies itself by sending a packet to the server upon login, I can automatically send users the correct resourcepack.

**Does OptiFine do this**
Optifine supports client branding when installed standalone, but doesn't do plugin messaging when installed with a mod loader ([yet](https://github.com/sp614x/optifine/issues/1631))

issues.title: [Idea] Sampling color from part textures in animation expressions
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
While looking at Fresh Moves and ETF, I realized a problem with sustainability for player models. As more and more features are added, more and more space is required.

This problem is unique to player models, since they're restricted to Mojang's definition of the player texture. You can't define a new texture, because then every player would use the same texture.

EMF especially suffers from this, as there's no way to "encode" data into the image like ETF does (and even that mod isn't perfect with it, but it's held to its reverse-compatibility promise).

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A way to sample the color of a part's texture in animation, perhaps as a function like `colorAt(some_part, x, y)`. The color itself would then have `r`, `g`, `b`, and `a` properties. Ideally, along with this feature would be bitwise operators (`&`, `|`, `^`, `~`) to enable packing efficiency, but it's not a hard requirement.

**Does OptiFine do this**
No.

**Additional context**
As mentioned in the summary of my problem, this mainly came from investigating Fresh Moves and ETF. Why I started investigating is because my player skin has unique 2x2 eyes that don't follow the assumption Fresh Moves makes. Fresh Moves is already packed to the brim, and there's not much space left that wouldn't conflict with ETF.

I figured that if there was a way for the model to check some pixels for their color, then it could be combined with other existing features, such as the `visible` property, to greatly reduce the space needed for highly dynamic player customization such as what Fresh Moves wants to do with eyes. Even a single pixel for encoding the eye type would allow all of the UVs for the eyes to collapse into a corner, sharing the same space, since the color could be used to set the `visible` property on the correct eye parts.

issues.title: [Idea] Nbt.Inventory issue and my idea to fix it
issues.body:
While creating a resource pack, I wanted to add custom armor to it and ran into a problem - mobs have 'ArmorItems' and 'HandItems' tags and it is very easy to determine the armor worn by mobs since each item is tied to a specific object in array, and these objects can be empty (ArmorItems.0 - boots, 1 - leggings, 2 - chestplate, 3 - helmet):
`nbt(ArmorItems.3.id, raw:minecraft:leather_helmet) && nbt(ArmorItems.3.tag.display.Name, raw:\"Bandana\")`

But the players doesn't have this option due to the fact that they uses the 'Inventory' tag in which new objects are added to array as slots are occupied.

Subsequently, I had an idea - in the game the 'data' command allows you to define an object containing a certain key, for example - an object with the key 'Slot:103b' (head slot):

`/data get entity @s Inventory[{Slot:103b}]`

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbd3cc9e-7ddf-451a-8c4e-421553947251)

This leads to my idea - being able to define an object in a list using a similar method, it might look like this:

`nbt.1.Inventory{Slot:103b}.id=raw:minecraft:leather_helmet`

 and same for nbt in emf cem animation:
`nbt(Inventory{Slot:103b}.id, raw:minecraft:leather_helmet)`

This will be useful for defining different tags of an item in a certain slot, such as its name.

issues.title: [Bug - models] "Require base model for variation" is outdated and doesn't work properly (Optifine compatibility)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**  
In the latest versions of Optifine, a base model for variations is only required if you don't have a .properties file. So it either need to have a base model or a .properties file to make variations work. In EMF, with the "Require base model - compatibility" option turned on (default settings), variations will only work if you have both, a base model and a .properties file. With the "Require base model - compatibility" option turned off, the base model is not mandatory, but the combination of base_model + variation2 + variation3 still won't work, unlike in Optifine.

To summarize:

**In Optifine:**
- model2 + model3 + model.properties **will work**
- base_model + model2 + model3 **will work** (a random model with equal chances is chosen, similar to how Random Entities work)
- model2 + model3 **won't work**
- base_model + model2 + model3 + model.properties **will obviously work**

**In EMF** (with "Require base model" enabled):
- base_model + model2 + model3 + model.properties **will only work**

**In EMF** (with "Require base model" disabled):
- model2 + model3 + model.properties **will work**
- base_model + model2 + model3 **won't work**
- base_model + model2 + model3 + model.properties **will work**

issues.title: [Bug - models] EMF doesn't support texture file path in .jem files properly. Optifine compatibility issue.
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
EMF doesn't properly support [Optifine file paths](https://optifine.readthedocs.io/syntax.html#paths-file-locations) in .jem files for the "texture" field. This means that setting the "texture" parameter to `"texture": "./textures/blastling.png"` or even `"texture": "./blastling.png"` causes the mod to load the model without a texture. It seems that EMF only loads textures when the "texture" parameter has no slashes and points to a texture in the same folder as the model, like `"texture": "blastling.png"`. 

This creates a compatibility issue, as Optifine loads textures located in the same folder as the model only when the "texture" parameter includes "./". 

As a result:
- A model with `"texture": "blastling.png"` will never have a texture with Optifine.
- A model with `"texture": "./blastling.png"` will never have a texture with EMF.

Additionally, EMF doesn't support placing model textures in subfolders, whereas Optifine supports this feature.

**List and link to broken resourcepacks**
[resourcepack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17002468/testtesttest2222.zip)

issues.title: [Idea] Some ideas for EMF
issues.body:
While I was creating my roleplay pack, I came up with several ideas for EMF

**[Idea 1] Separate armor parts into 4 different models and other armor ideas**
My idea is to separate the armor parts into 4 models (helmet.jem, chestplate.jem, leggings.jem, boots.jem) and add new properties instead of mob dependent models to avoid creating duplicate models.

The models of the helmet, chestplate and boots will be identical so that armor with extra parts can be created.
Additional parts will initially be hidden, but can be enabled using <part>.visible 
For example, chestplate - jacket with hood on the head:
	"head.visible": "body.visible"

Which mob is wearing an armor will be determined by the "wearer" property.
	wearer.1=zombie husk
	wearer.2=minecraft:skeleton minecraft:stray

Which armor piece the mob is wearing will be determined by the "item" property.
	item.1=iron_helmet minecraft:diamond_helmet

Using the "itemName" property you can determine the name of the wearing item (also will work with regex:, iregex:, pattern: and ipattern:).
It will be easier for creating packs, since the player and mobs use different formats
In 1.21 nbt tags were replaced with components and some components have different names (and they may change in future versions)
	itemName.1=Military helmet

**[Idea 2] Leather armor overlay texture (not tinted) can be specified using "texture_overlay":"<filename>" in a model.**
Example:
	"texture": "textures/models/custom/jacket.png",
	"texture_overlay": "textures/models/custom/jacket_overlay.png"

**[Idea 3] ETF armor/elytra should override Cit Resewn armor/elytra because Cit Resewn doesn't work with textures in not-vanilla folders.**

**[Idea 4] Variable names for texture animation**
Can be used to animate textures like breeze wind
If the animation goes beyond the texture then the texture will loop
	
For Box UV cubes:
tu - Translation along the u axis.
tv - Translation along the v axis.
	

For Per-face UV cubes:
tun - Translation of the north face along the u axis.
tue - Translation of the east face along the u axis.
tus - Translation of the south face along the u axis.
tuw - Translation of the west face along the u axis.
tuu - Translation of the up face along the u axis.
tud - Translation of the down face along the u axis.
tvn - Translation of the north face along the v axis.
tve - Translation of the east face along the v axis.
tvs - Translation of the south face along the v axis.
tvw - Translation of the west face along the v axis.
tvu - Translation of the up face along the v axis.
tvd - Translation of the down face along the v axis.
sun - Scale the north face along the u axis.
sue - Scale the east face along the u axis.
sus - Scale the south face along the u axis.
suw - Scale the west face along the u axis.
suu - Scale the up face along the u axis.
sud - Scale the down face along the u axis.
svn - Scale the north face along the v axis.
sve - Scale the east face along the v axis.
svs - Scale the south face along the v axis.
svw - Scale the west face along the v axis.
svu - Scale the up face along the v axis.
svd - Scale the down face along the v axis.

**[Idea 5] Single-sided cubes**
"double-sided" definition for model parts will make it possible to make single-sided parts (like block models)
"double-sided": <true|false> (defaulf is true)
Example:
"id": "flower",
"translate": [0, 0, 0],
"double-sided": false
		
**[Idea 6] Cubes without shade**
"shade" definition for model parts that will allow you to disable the shade for the cubes (like in block models)
"shade": <true|false> (defaulf is true)
Example:
"id": "flame",
"translate": [0, 0, 0],
"shade": false

**[Idea 7] Applying color on a model parts**
New variable names will allow you to apply color to the cubes using animations
red    Overlays with red   color
green  Overlays with green color
blue   Overlays with blue  color
alpha  Translucency of a overlay colors
Setting all to 0 disables all color overlays
Example:
"body.red": "if(is_hurt, 0.7, 0)",
"body.alpha": "if(is_hurt, 0.5, 0)"

**[Idea 8] Camera rotation render parameters**
"camera_rot_x" and "camera_rot_y" - parameters that will returns player's camera rotation
Can be used with previous two ideas to create fake particles
(player_rot_<x|y> returns rotation of a player's head, not a camera's and sometimes it doesn't look right with mods that allow you to move it separated)
![player rotation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b023b7f8-4ec4-4906-82f4-d8bd8792cac2)


**[Idea 9] Player (and Player Armor) exclusive animation variable**
Variable "**pixel.u.v.channel**" will return color/alpha channel value of a specific pixel of the player's skin (0-255)
u - defines the horizontal position of a pixel on the texture
v - defines the vertical position of a pixel on the texture
channel - determines exactly what channel value will be returned (red, green, blue or alpha)
Example:
"body.sy": "if(pixel.0.16.alpha == 123, 1/12 * (8 + min(pixel.0.16.red, 4)), 1)",
"left_ear.visible": "pixel.3.16.red==1 && pixel.3.16.alpha==123"

issues.title: [Bug] Exceptions are silenced during model update
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
I have a server-side mod which adds custom data to villagers NBT. I recently fixed an issue with it that caused performance drops in singleplayer, when combined with Fresh Animations. While investigating this, I found that my NBT code would throw exceptions if called from the Render Thread. However, no corresponding errors were present in the logs.
I believe EMF catches and discards these exceptions without logging them.

Due to the nature of my mod (server-side and rarely ever does anything), I might have never suspected it could be involved in render-related issues, had someone else not made the connection. Even if printing the errors would result in a spam, this is preferable to no error at all. Being able to see them would have enabled me to identify and fix the issue much sooner.

Throwing was the first, and therefore only, thing that my mod did, meaning throwing is on its own enough to tank performances. For this reason, I woud not consider any exception to be benign.

**Mod list:**
 - Minecraft: 1.21
 - EMF: 2.1.3
 - ETF: 6.13
 - Fresh Animations: 1.9.2
 - Shifting Wares: 2.2.1 (**NOT** 2.2.2 which has the issue fixed)

**To Reproduce**
Summon a Villager and look at it. 
Whenever EMF refreshes the villager's NBT, Shifting Wares will call `VillagerEntity::getOffers` on the Render Thread, which throws an exception.
No errors are visible in the log.

Possibly related to #95. It looks very similar to what I observed with my own mod.

issues.title: [Bug - models] Custom mob heads in GUI
issues.body:
The mod seem to be really not liking mob heads being rendered ub GUI or first-person hands, if not tile entities entirely. In short, in my resourcepacks (which are not public anywhere, I'm sorry).
I have some replacements for the mobs and their heads, also including player. And it seems to be rather a rendering problem of some sort, because in some cases it renders them as expected, but in some it just makes them rather invisible or partly black. In case of mob heads, they just disappear whenever you highlight them or... highlight some other specific tile entity items? Also when grabbing specifically the trident in your hand, their inner parts are just going... black...
In case of player models which I have fully modelled as little "chibi players", they have some custom conditional animations, but with this mod they just change their poses at random moments because I made them animate differently in different conditions, mostly by stacking one inside each other like "if(is_in_gui, true1, if(is_in_hand, true2, if(is_on_head, true3, if(is_in_item_frame, true4, false))))". But for this mod these animations just kind of... randomly stack together, especially considering that for the most part they're slightly raised upwards, which should only be the case when you wear them on your head (they're just sitting on top of your head), slightly floating to left and right, which should only happen in GUI, and also frequently changing poses between general "sitting" one and the one that should be when held in the hand (the animation of them "climbing" on your arm). I think in this case it's just a problem of missing predicates or not exactly following them how it should.

Here's how it usually looks with Optifine. No rendering errors, no animation stacking, sorry for low quality, GitHub kinda made me do that.
https://github.com/Traben-0/Entity_Model_Features/assets/82406050/4f5027c3-2230-408d-9b07-7c2f365580a7

Here's how the same packs currently look with your mods.

issues.title: [Bug - models] Custom models turn invisible when texture file is in custom directory
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When a .jem model has a texture reference, that is not in the directory where the default texture would be, the entire model turns invisible
(sometimes only when also using Iris shaders - happens with BSL, Sildurs, and Builders QOL - probably many more)

https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/nautilus3d
Take a look at the Trident in the current version of my Pack Nautilus3D. I noticed that problem when updating to 1.20.4.
I managed to fix it by removing the texture reference from the .jem model, and moving the texture file to _minecraft/textures/entity/trident.png_
This is the Nautilus3D commit fixing the issue:
https://github.com/FabianMPunkt/Nautilus3D/commit/28bf4973b4806b5f3e2a7d76b6d93f8607774941

It should be visible.

issues.title: [Bug - models] multiple textures in a single .jem file are overlaying instead of replacing each other
issues.body:
Hello there!
I'm working on a resource pack that turns villagers into player-like humans, which I want to be compatible with any player skin so I added the brim of the hats (like the straw hat of the farmer villager) as a separate texture in the .jem file.
the brim texture is a 16x16 texture that is completely filled.
The villager model has a block for the brim, which has a transparent texture on the normal villager, which gets replaced if they have a job with a brim, like a farmer via a .properties file.
The problem is, that the textures get layered on top of each other, instead of getting replaced.

In Optifine (HD_U_I5 for 1.20.1) it's supposed to look like this:
![Screenshot 2023-12-17 130211](https://github.com/Traben-0/Entity_Model_Features/assets/93039234/e3dfed4a-47b6-417f-9282-1a92b52da4e5)
but with EMF it looks like this:
![Screenshot 2023-12-17 143741](https://github.com/Traben-0/Entity_Model_Features/assets/93039234/d9f96b10-8d10-4aad-ac77-f30bbf3f524b)

As you can see, the whole texture of the villager is rendered on the brim with the separate brim texture layered under it. (you can't see it on the left side but there is a tiny pink dot inside the head, which is the mostly transparent texture for the invisible brim.)
This happens both, with the regular boxes method and the extra, separate .jpm file method


 - Minecraft Version: [e.g. 1.20.4]
 - EMF version: [e.g. 1.2]
 - ETF version: [5.0]
 - loaded with Quilt loader version: [0.20.0]


Additional stuff:
With sodium 0.5.5 and iris shaders 1.6.14 it flips the order, which is kinda curious:
![Screenshot 2023-12-17 130807](https://github.com/Traben-0/Entity_Model_Features/assets/93039234/e2e441b5-5ae2-4b7e-b39c-07a328ec0edf)
I also encountered some other issues while experimenting where the whole model was covered with brim texture, which obviously also shouldn't happen but I don't know how to replicate it. I still wanted to include that here for completion's sake.
![Untitled](https://github.com/Traben-0/Entity_Model_Features/assets/93039234/27d37876-d4a1-4ef6-80ab-0824f39a32b9)

issues.title: Notice: EMF 1.0 and old issues
issues.body:
EMF 1.0 is practically a different mod to the last beta 0.2.13 and the old private alpha,
Almost the entire model creation code is different and almost all issues reported using old beta versions will be irrelevant going forwards. (especially if it is about broken models)

With that being said, many GitHub issues have been left mostly ignored by me during developement if I felt the issue was something that I expected would get resolved passively during development.

With 1.0's release I will be going through these older issues in the coming months to actually address and weed out which issues are still relevant or not.

# tl;dr What to do
If you have an issue with version 1.0 or later **PLEASE** make a new issue rather than comment in an issue thread started during the beta.
I encourage you to #mention the old issue thread if it is relevant to your new 1.0 issue instead.

**all issues after this post should be for the release version only**

issues.title: Models/textures for various modded mobs appear broken ( NOT ACTUALLY CAUSED BY EMF, ISSUE CLOSED)
issues.body:
EDIT:
While testing to see if the issue persisted with version 1.0 I found out it was not in fact caused by EMF, but Max's better mobs. I could have sworn I didn't have that installed on my test profile when I made this post but either way the issue does not appear to be caused by EMF. Closing this post.

When Entity Model Features is installed various mobs from a handful of other mods appear with broken textures/models. The mobs I have seen affected are as follows:
- Skeleton creeper from "The Graveyard"
- Legionnaire from "It Takes a Pillage"
- Archer from "It Takes a Pillage"
- Vampire from "Supernatural"

I tested these mods all individually and together with Entity Model Features and it seems that it is not always the same mobs that are broken. The first time I noticed this it was just the Archer from It Takes a Pillage, and after some test worlds and reinstallations all of a sudden the Archer was normal and the Legionnaire was broken. I only have pictures of the skeleton creeper and the legionnaire as those were the only two affected during my final testing and I cannot figure out what causes it to change which models are broken.  

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Download latest 1.19.2 release of "The Graveyard" (forge) 
2. Download latest 1.19.2 release of "It Takes a Pillage" (forge) 
3. Download lateset 1.19.2 release of "Supernatural" (forge)
4. Enter game and create world
5. Spawn listed mobs to see normal appearances
6. Download latest 1.19.2 release of "Entity Model Features" (forge)
7. Re-enter world and see which mobs are affected
8. "Delete Entity Model Features" 
9. Re-enter world to confirm that mobs are no longer affected

**Expected behavior**
Mobs added by other mods to appear with the proper models and textures

**Screenshots**

![2023-09-14_19 27 16](https://github.com/Traben-0/Entity_Model_Features/assets/144986357/1a4aec9e-7143-4069-881c-1007fcf1ed93)

issues.title: [Todo] Log instances of "Try to prevent EMF models being overridden" occurring, to warn users of crash risk in mods not expecting it, and leave a presence of the cause in the log.
issues.body:
Currently, EMF is replacing models created by other mods. This has the _horrible_ side-effect that EMF will cause crashes in other mods' code for any players that try to use it together with Mine Little Pony, and possibly any other mods that add unique player models.


Upon my own investigating, I found the "Try to prevent EMF models being overridden" setting in "Options & Fixes" where it is enabled for a fresh install. It's my opinion that any setting like this that can lead to game crashes should rather always be disabled by default.

Thank you.

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When playing a 1.18.2 modpack (e.g. Better Minecraft, other Private Modpacks, etc) with [Entity Texture Features](https://modrinth.com/mod/entitytexturefeatures), and using [HIDYK's REALM](https://modrinth.com/resourcepack/hidyksrealm). *Yes,* obviously.

**Additional context**

issues.title: I'm the first. Make a transitional transparency for for mobs at the boundary of their rendering.
issues.body:
I saw the Fade spawn animation feature in Alpha and decided needed to go further.
Perhaps this is already implemented by some mod, but I do not know about it.
But here's an idea.

- For example: rendering a mob in 96 blocks.
- When he are in 96 blocks. The mob appears, but has a completely transparent texture, as the player gets closer to the mob the texture transparency increases to 100% on 90 blocks.
- And vice versa, as they are removed.
